advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Either wire a production close-gate caller to PlanValidityProfile.CLOSE or remove the unused member (it duplicates DRIFT_REFRESH behavior).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pin_health.py:17: `    CLOSE = "close"`
search for `PlanValidityProfile.CLOSE` / `profile=` in src/rebar returns only DEFAULT and DRIFT_REFRESH usages; CLOSE appears only in tests/unit/test_plan_material_pin_health_heldout.py:103
In compute_validity the freshness branch is gated `if profile is PlanValidityProfile.DEFAULT`, so CLOSE and DRIFT_REFRESH take an identical path (attest.py:563)
advisory.finding: PlanValidityProfile.CLOSE is defined (and exercised only by tests) but is never selected by any production caller; it also produces behavior identical to DRIFT_REFRESH (both merely skip the code-freshness block), so it is a dead/unwired enum member.
scenarios: A future close-gate caller assumes CLOSE has distinct semantics and wires it expecting different behavior than DRIFT_REFRESH.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile derive_health's fingerprint error handling with current_material_fingerprint's None-on-error contract so the io/reducer failure_kind path reflects actual production behavior (or make the seam actually raise).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pin_health.py:112-119: `current = fingerprint(...)` guarded by `except OSError` / `except Exception` setting fingerprint_failed + emitting 'io'/'reducer'
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py:766-797: current_material_fingerprint wraps its body in `except Exception ... return None` (never raises)
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pin_health.py:122-125: when current is None and not fingerprint_failed, _warn_unreadable does a SECOND show_ticket read to classify failure_kind

The 'io'/'reducer' failure_kind emitted from lines 116/119 is only reachable via the test monkeypatch that makes current_material_fingerprint raise (test_plan_material_pin_health_heldout.py test_unreadable_target_warns...)
advisory.finding: In derive_health the except OSError / except Exception handlers wrapping the fingerprint() call are effectively unreachable in production because the injected fingerprint (current_material_fingerprint) catches all exceptions internally and returns None; a genuinely unreadable target is therefore classified as 'stale-pin-missing' via the redundant _warn_unreadable re-read rather than emitting the 'io'/'reducer' failure_kind those handlers produce.
scenarios: A related ticket's material cannot be read due to a real I/O error in production: the pin is reported stale-pin-missing and (under enforcement) invalidates the attestation, while the failure_kind='io' path the tests assert never runs.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the AST/source-grep in test_compute_validity_callers.py with a behavioral assertion (call compute_validity / the wired callers and assert on returned mapping keys and profile effects), removing the change-detector coupling to implementation source shape.
evidence: `root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "src" / "rebar"` then `tree = ast.parse(path.read_text(...))` — the assertion target is the parsed SOURCE UNDER TEST, not its behavior
`assert any(isinstance(consumer, ast.Subscript) or (... consumer.attr == "get" ...) for consumer in consumers), f"{path}:{node.lineno} does not consume validity by named key"`

Litmus (Rule 4): renaming the `validity`/`v` local or restructuring consumption at attest.py:164/750 or completion.py:176 leaves behavior identical but changes the AST this test inspects — a change-detector, not a behavior-verifier
advisory.finding: test_compute_validity_callers.py is a source-grepping change-detector: it ast.parse()s the source under test (src/rebar/**/*.py) and asserts on the AST shape of every compute_validity call site (that the result is consumed via subscript or `.get`, never tuple-unpacked), rather than asserting any observable behavior. It would break on a behavior-preserving refactor (renaming the assigned local, restructuring how the mapping is consumed, moving the call) with no change to program behavior.
scenarios: A future refactor renames a local or changes how compute_validity's dict is consumed while preserving behavior; the test fails despite no regression

evidence: Diff adds: `except ManifestFormatError: plan_health = {"pin_status": "malformed-pin", ...}` and `if plan_health["pin_status"] == "malformed-pin" and enforced: return {... "verdict": "malformed-pin", ...}`
search_files 'malformed-pin' under tests/unit returned no matches
test_compute_validity_enforces_or_advises_same_health only asserts verdict == 'stale-pin-drift'
advisory.finding: No test exercises compute_validity's new enforced 'malformed-pin' early-return branch (manifest_pins raises ManifestFormatError while enforce_plan_material_pins is on), which returns {valid: False, verdict: 'malformed-pin'}. The heldout suite covers only stale-pin-drift enforcement.

advisory.finding: resign's ReviewedRelatedMaterialError -> {pin_status: 'malformed-pin'} fallback branch is untested. The resign enforcement test uses a valid-but-drifted reviewed_related_material payload (stale-pin-drift), so the except path at resign.py:119-120 that refuses re-sign on a malformed sidecar under enforcement never executes.
